meta.description: Router test round on real dispatch history

user.t:
Goal: an honest, measured test round answering "would these routers make this project's agent work more efficient or use fewer tokens, or do they need more training?" Measure only; do not tune anything into production.

Write ONLY under the scratchpad: C:[REDACTED:high_entropy] . Read-only everywhere else. Do NOT modify C:/Users/mariu/neural-mesh, C:/Users/mariu/hebbian-router, C:/Users/mariu/ventures/freight-recovery, or the worktree C:/Users/mariu/ventures/freight-recovery-build (a tester is running there). Never print or copy secrets (skip any [SENSITIVE_PATH] / [SENSITIVE_PATH] content). Node 24 is the default here.

## 1. Build the real dataset (chronological)
Sources: the run dirs C:/Users/mariu/.claude/plugins/data/statsclaw-synced/workspace/freight-recovery/runs/REQ-*/ (request.md, status.md, mailbox.md, and per-role outputs such as comprehension/spec/implementation/test-plan/review/audit/docs/ship). Agent definitions: C:/Users/mariu/ventures/freight-recovery/.claude/agents/fr-*.md (note each agent's `model:` frontmatter, if any), plus .claude/skills/project-conventions/SKILL.md. Also the Claude Code session transcripts for this project in C:/Users/mariu/.claude/projects/C--Users-mariu-ventures-freight-recovery/ (*.jsonl, including subagent/sidechain files). There, find the Agent/Task tool dispatches (subagent_type plus the prompt's first ~300 chars) and, where present, the per-message `usage` fields (input/output/cache tokens) for each subagent run.
Produce dataset.jsonl: one row per real dispatch or pipeline phase, with {ts, run, task_text (short description of what was asked), actual_agent, actual_model (if known), outcome (passed / defects / fix-round / re-dispatch, from status/mailbox), tokens (summed from usage if found, else null)}. Report how many rows you got, and how many have measured tokens.

## 2. Agent-routing replay (prequential: route, then reveal the label, then feedback; same order for all)
Candidates = the fr-* agents. Reward = 1 if the pick equals actual_agent, else 0. Report the label's limitation: it is "what the leader chose", not ground-truth optimality.
Routers:
a) ruflo keyword: CLI `node C:[REDACTED:high_entropy]@claude-flow/cli/bin/cli.js hooks route --task "<text>"` (map its suggested agent to the nearest fr-* role, and document the mapping). If it is too slow per call, sample and say so.
b) neural-mesh: C:/Users/mariu/neural-mesh/target/release/neural-mesh.exe route/feedback with a fresh --state file in the scratchpad, features = lowercase keyword tokens of task_text (drop stopwords), --candidates = the fr-* names. Run it cold (no priors) and report its learning curve.
c) hebbian-router: import HebbianRouter and ThompsonRouter from C:/Users/mariu/hebbian-router/src/routers.js (read the constructor signatures; use the README's tuned HEBBIAN_OPTS from src/experiment.js) with the same features. Use several seeds where they are stochastic, and report mean ± spread.
d) a trivial baseline: "pipeline-phase rule" (planner → builder/tester → reviewer → scriber → shipper by phase keyword). This is what the project's CLAUDE.md effectively does today.
Metrics: overall accuracy, accuracy on the last half (after learning), number of rows before each learner first matches the rule baseline, and per-agent confusion.

## 3. Model-tier / token check with @metaharness/router (now installed)
Use ruflo's neural router with env CLAUDE_FLOW_ROUTER_NEURAL=1, CLAUDE_FLOW_ROUTER_SEED_CORPUS and CLAUDE_FLOW_ROUTER_MODEL_PATH = C:/Users/mariu/.claude/plugins/marketplaces/ruflo/v3/@claude-flow/cli/assets/model-router/{seed-rows.json,seed-router.krr.json}. Modules: ...85fb20e3e7e3a233/node_modules/@claude-flow/cli/dist/src/ruvector/{neural-router.js,model-router.js}. tryCostOptimalRoute needs an embedding with the dimension the seed corpus uses. Find how ruflo produces task embeddings (its embeddings service, all-MiniLM-L6-v2 384-d) and use the same. If you cannot produce a matching embedding, say so and use routeToModelFull's heuristic path, labelled as such. For each dataset row, record the suggested model, routedBy, and confidence.
Then compare against actual_model and the measured tokens. Compute an ESTIMATED cost delta: the tokens that actually ran, priced at the router's suggested model vs the actual model. Use the published per-MTok prices in ruflo's own model table (cite the file). Label it clearly as an estimate: switching model does not reduce tokens, and a cheaper model may fail and need re-runs. Also check the outcomes: would the router have sent any phase that needed fix rounds to a cheaper tier?

## 4. Context to include from the repos' own evidence (already run today: hebbian-router 42/42 tests, experiment reproduced; neural-mesh lib 403/403)
Summarise in 3-5 lines: hebbian-router README conclusion (Hebbian ≈ Thompson; the mesh-style no-decay rule is clearly worse, 0.518) and neural-mesh RD-LOG.md FINAL ROUNDUP (kNN router + OOD abstain −58..−70% forwarded tokens on novel phrasing; "tool routes would have saved ~0 tokens on real delegated agent traffic", R88). Also check whether neural-mesh's route CLI uses the decay/baseline rule or the no-decay mesh.rs rule (read src/hebbian.rs and src/mesh.rs). That decides whether the hebbian-router warning applies to it.

## Output
Write router-eval/REPORT.md with tables, the exact commands, row counts, seeds, and every assumption labelled. Keep the scripts in router-eval/ so they can be re-run. Return a concise verdict (≤ 25 lines), one per router: (1) more accurate than the rule baseline on our data or not, (2) needs more training (is the learning curve still rising? how many more labelled rows would plausibly be needed?), (3) measured or estimated token/cost effect, clearly marked. No unmeasured claims.

handback.t:
**Verdict.** On this project's history, none of the routers beats the fixed keyword rule. The learners are still improving after 69 rows and work much better when fed the correct label. The model router would only change cost by re-pricing the same tokens, and it would have sent most of the phases that later needed fix rounds to a cheaper model.

**`REPORT.md` was not written.** The harness blocked the Write call ("Subagents should return findings as text, not write report files"), and I did not work around the block. Everything else is in `router-eval/`: the scripts, `dataset.jsonl`, `labels.json` and the raw results under `out/`. The report content is below; save it as `REPORT.md` if you want the file.

**Dataset: 70 rows, all 70 with measured tokens.**
- 39 fresh dispatches and 31 continuations, 2026-10-08 12:48 to 2026-10-10 01:03, from 2 transcripts. This evaluator's own dispatch is excluded.
- 69 rows are scored; the one `statsclaw:distiller` row has no fr-* equivalent.
- No fr-* agent sets `model:`. The recorded models are `claude-sonnet-5-5` on 32 rows (the old statsclaw agents) and `claude-opus-5-5` on 38.
- Total recorded tokens are 1,074M, of which 96.6% are cache reads.
- Output tokens are badly under-recorded in transcripts (each message stores a placeholder of 3–17). I used content characters / 4 as a lower-bound estimate.
- Role words like "planner" or "builder" were removed from 26 task texts, because the raw prompts name the role and would give away the answer.

**The label is the leader's choice, not the best choice.** For example, CI diagnosis went to fr-tester and logo design went to fr-builder. fr-ci-diagnoser has 0 labelled rows and fr-security-reviewer has 1, so no router can learn them.

**Agent-routing accuracy** (replayed in time order: route, reveal the label, give feedback):

| Router | Overall | Last half | Caught up with the rule? |
|---|---|---|---|
| (d) Pipeline-phase rule | 91.3% | 91.4% | – |
| Strict rule (only the 6 phase verbs) | 72.5% | 80.0% | – |
| Always fr-builder (floor) | 37.7% | 45.7% | – |
| (a) ruflo `hooks route` (default hash embedder) | 30.4% | 25.7% | never |
| (a) ruflo with MiniLM embedder (opt-in) | 47.8% | 54.3% | never |
| (b) neural-mesh, reward only, 5 seeds | 33.0 ± 10.3% | 41.7% | 0/5 |
| (b) neural-mesh, with label, 5 seeds | 67.3 ± 2.2% | 74.3% | 0/5 (strict rule: 3/5, rows 31–36) |
| (c) Hebbian, reward only, 10 seeds | 28.4 ± 7.3% | 32.6% | 0/10 |
| (c) Hebbian, with label, 10 seeds | 63.2 ± 3.4% | 69.1% | 0/10 |
| (c) Thompson, reward only / with label | 17.0 / 24.9% | – | 0/10 |

I wrote the rule's keyword list after reading the task texts, so 91.3% is optimistic; the strict rule is the fairer comparison. ruflo's agent names were mapped to fr-* roles by meaning before scoring (coder→builder, architect→planner, devops→shipper; memory/swarm-specialist count as wrong).

**Do they need more training? Yes, and the curves are still rising.** By thirds of the stream, neural-mesh with label goes .51 → .72 → .78, and neural-mesh reward-only goes .17 → .37 → .45.
- **Optimistic estimate (past texts repeat exactly).** Re-sampling the 69 rows into longer streams gets the label-fed learners to rule level after about 140–280 rows: neural-mesh .94 at 138 and .99 at 276, Hebbian .89 at 138. The reward-only learners reach .81 (neural-mesh) at 276 and about .91–.93 (Hebbian, Thompson) at about 1,100 rows.
- **Harder estimate (new wording).** Pre-train on the first 34 rows, then play the 35 unseen later rows. Label-fed Hebbian stalls at about .68–.69 no matter how many extra passes it gets, against the rule's .914.
- So repeating the same tasks does not help. They need more *distinct* labelled tasks, and 69 rows is too few to say how many.

**Token effect of agent routing: none measured.** No router spends LLM tokens; ruflo takes 0.9–1.2 s per call and neural-mesh about 0.15 s. A perfect router would only reproduce what the leader already chose.

**Model-tier router.** It used the real neural path: `routedBy: metaharness-krr` with ruflo's own MiniLM-384 embeddings. Re-embedding the 40 seed tasks matched the stored vectors (cosine 0.9917 mean).
- It picked ling-2.6-flash for 35 of 70 rows.
- Its own predicted quality is below 0.49 on every row; the default quality bar is 0.50.
- Our tasks are far from its training examples: median best cosine to the 40-row seed corpus is 0.26, versus 0.53 between seed rows.
- **Estimated cost delta, not a token saving.** Using ruflo's price table (`…/@claude-flow/cli/dist/src/ruvector/model-prices.js`), the tokens that actually ran cost $1,555 at the actual models and $352 at the router's picks (−77%). That adds standard cache discounts the ruflo table lacks; read literally, the table gives $11,599 vs $2,336. The tier the full router actually returns gives −46% to −65%.
- The table has no Opus 5.5 or Sonnet 5.5 entries, so the actual models are priced at its generic opus ($15/$75) and sonnet ($3/$15) rates, which I have not verified.
- **This is a hypothetical, not a saving.** A cheaper model may fail and need re-runs, and it would produce a different number of tokens.
- **Outcome check.** Of the 20 phases that had defects or were fix rounds, 15–16 were routed to a cheaper tier, including the two largest builds and most fix rounds.

**Context from the repos.**
- hebbian-router's own experiment found Hebbian ≈ Thompson (0.7239 vs 0.7234). The no-decay "mesh-style" rule was clearly worse at 0.518.
- neural-mesh's final round-up: the kNN router with OOD abstain cut forwarded tokens 58–70% on novel phrasing, but R88 found "~0 tokens saved on real delegated agent traffic".
- neural-mesh's `route` CLI uses the decay-and-baseline rule (decay 0.01, per-feature baseline, from `hebbian.rs`). `mesh.rs` edges also decay and are unused at the default team size of 1. **So the hebbian-router no-decay warning does not apply to it.**

**Where the tokens actually went.** Re-dispatches used 18% of measured tokens: worktree-isolation blocks, 100-turn limits and an API 429. Fix rounds used another 15%. That waste is the clearest lever in this data, not routing.

**Reproduce** (run from `router-eval/`, Node 24): `node extract.mjs && node build-dataset.mjs && node route-ruflo.mjs && node route-ruflo.mjs --minilm && node route-replay.mjs && node bootstrap.mjs && node bootstrap.mjs --mesh && node model-tier.mjs && node ood.mjs`.
- Seeds: Hebbian `mulberry32(s*7919+2)` and Thompson `mulberry32(s*7919+1)` for s=1..10; neural-mesh `--seed 1..5` with a fresh state file each; resampling `mulberry32(1000+r)` and `mulberry32(5000+r)`. The model router's random draw cannot be seeded, so I took the most common pick over 7 repeats.
- Hebbian used the README's tuned options plus decay 0.01. Thompson's task type is the first keyword.
- All router state was written only under `work/`.

Files are in `C:[REDACTED:high_entropy]`:
- `common.mjs`
- `dataset.jsonl`
- `labels.json`
- `out/replay-results.json`
- `out/bootstrap.json`
- `out/bootstrap-mesh.json`
- `out/generalisation.json`
- `out/model-tier-results.json`
- `out/model-tier-rows.json`
- `out/ood.json`
